[README](https://github.com/asavis/chess_accuracy#) - [MIT license](https://github.com/asavis/chess_accuracy#) # Chess Game Accuracy Analysis Script [Permalink: Chess Game Accuracy Analysis Script](https://github.com/asavis/chess_accuracy#chess-game-accuracy-analysis-script) This script processes chess PGN (Portable Game Notation) data to compute the average centipawn loss and a mean of volatility-weighted mean and harmonic mean (Accuracy) for both players. ## Requirements [Permalink: Requirements](https://github.com/asavis/chess_accuracy#requirements) - Python 3.6 or higher - `chess` Python library - Stockfish chess engine (compatible version for your system) ## Installation [Permalink: Installation](https://github.com/asavis/chess_accuracy#installation) 1. Install Python 3.6+ from [python.org](https://www.python.org/). 2. Install the `chess` library using pip: ``` pip install python-chess ``` 3. Download the Stockfish engine from the official [Stockfish website](https://stockfishchess.org/download/) and place it in a known directory. ## Usage [Permalink: Usage](https://github.com/asavis/chess_accuracy#usage) Basic usage requires specifying the analysis depth, number of threads, and path to the Stockfish engine. You can input PGN data either from a file or directly as a string: ### From a File [Permalink: From a File](https://github.com/asavis/chess_accuracy#from-a-file) ``` python chess_accuracy.py 16 2 /path/to/stockfish -file=/path/to/game.pgn ``` ### From a PGN String [Permalink: From a PGN String](https://github.com/asavis/chess_accuracy#from-a-pgn-string) ``` python chess_accuracy.py 16 2 /path/to/stockfish -pgn="1.e4 e5 2.Nf3 Nc6 3.Bb5 a6" ``` ### Using Standard Input [Permalink: Using Standard Input](https://github.com/asavis/chess_accuracy#using-standard-input) You can also pipe PGN data into the script: ``` cat /path/to/game.pgn | python chess_accuracy.py 18 2 /path/to/stockfish ``` ### Verbose Output [Permalink: Verbose Output](https://github.com/asavis/chess_accuracy#verbose-output) For detailed output, including move-by-move analysis, add the `-verbose` flag at the end: ``` python chess_accuracy.py 16 2 /path/to/stockfish -file=/path/to/game.pgn -verbose ``` ## Output [Permalink: Output](https://github.com/asavis/chess_accuracy#output) The script outputs the average centipawn loss and harmonic mean of accuracy for both players, formatted as follows: ``` Average centipawn loss (White), Accuracy (White), Average centipawn loss (Black), Accuracy (Black): 44, 84, 15, 95 ``` For verbose mode, additional details for each move are printed to the console. ## License [Permalink: License](https://github.com/asavis/chess_accuracy#license) MIT © 2025 Alexander Stasiv ## About Chess Game Accuracy Analysis Script ### Topics [chess](https://github.com/topics/chess "Topic: chess") [accuracy](https://github.com/topics/accuracy "Topic: accuracy") [stockfish](https://github.com/topics/stockfish "Topic: stockfish") [centipawn-loss](https://github.com/topics/centipawn-loss "Topic: centipawn-loss") ### Resources [Readme](https://github.com/asavis/chess_accuracy#readme-ov-file) ### License [MIT license](https://github.com/asavis/chess_accuracy#MIT-1-ov-file) ### Uh oh!
